Oh Terraria, where do I even begin...

I've been a console plebian for my entire life until recently, and have only [i]just started[/i] to experience modding for the first time after moving to PC.
Whenever I was playing on my Xbox pre-1.4 console, I was hooked onto mastering this game start to finish. Even now, going through the early game phase that everyone dreads, I still enjoy dying over and over again in Master Mode because of that sense of exploration and wonder that has never truly went away despite my years of playing this game.
I admit that I have yet to keep up with 1.4.5, but as I pick up Terraria again, it makes me relive my childhood days being trapped in the house during a winter storm where I had no internet, and the only game I could play was Terraria 1.3 on the disc.
So needless to say, my hours are underlogged.
But if you're experiencing this game for the first time; I'm jealous of you. You have so much to learn and explore [i](including myself with my limited modding experience)[/i] and I hope that you can enjoy Terraria as much as I have. It will involve a lot of wiki surfing yes, and it will involve a lot of dying, but I promise you that the fun, challenge, and excitement has yet to begin. 

I truly and completely have fell in love with Terraria and it will forever be my favorite game.
[b][i]Happy exploring, my fellow Terrarians![/i][/b]

claims.claim: Reviewers report that some end-game items and events rely heavily on luck, requiring hours of waiting and grinding.

citations.review_text:
[h2] Standout Positives: [/h2]
- [b] Replayability [/b]: Terraria is one of those games you could realistically play and enjoy for thousands of hours in vanilla before you start looking for mods. There are so many different play styles and gameplay options it's insane. 
- [b] Flexibility [/b]: From the building mechanics to exploring, combat, character classes and difficulty, I genuinely believe there is something here for everybody.  
- [b] Boss Fights [/b]: The bosses in Terraria are surprisingly fun, especially on the harder difficulty worlds. In the early-game they're a bit slow but later on they can become pretty intense and cinematic! 
- [b] Fun Factor [/b]: Very generally, this game is just super fun. For both solo and multiplayer worlds, sitting down to play Terraria is always a great time (although I have to be careful when I play since it's super addicting). 

[h2] Standout Negatives: [/h2]
- [b] RNG Mechanics [/b]: A lot of end-game items and events come down to getting lucky which can get a bit frustrating if you're trying to max out your character/get all the achievements. And when I say "getting lucky," I mean it; it can take hours of waiting/grinding to get a single item.

[h2] Overall... [/h2] 
I mean, it's Terraria. I've yet to find anyone who genuinely hates this game. Even though some areas can be a bit grindy, you can customize your experience to fit exactly what you want in the moment. It's so much fun and I highly recommend it.
if you get into this game good luck ur spending over 20 hours trying to get 1 item for the class you picked

Simply put, Terraria is one of if not the most enjoyable action sandbox game money can buy.
To explain the rough idea of Terraria it runs off of player curiosity and the natural urge to explore new things, you'll find yourself asking "What's this? or "Who's that?" or "Does this hurt me?" every moment you play. I'm aware of the turn offs such as "It's too grindy" or "There's no guide to progression" but thats the entire intent of Terraria, it's built for you to learn on your own through exploration, stay in certain areas to kill certain enemies for specific drops needed to progress. In nature this is a grindy and long-winded game but for all the right reasons. I'll keep it concise in a bullet point list as to what Terrarias progression looks like to the average player (my own time played totals to around 1.1k hours on Steam but 2k more on other devices).

Early Game (Pre-Boss):
- Make housing using the beginner tools provided
- Delve into the naturally spawning caves in search of loot
- Further explore each side of your world to find the two important early parts of Terraria (the jungle and the dungeon - they spawn on opposite sides of the world to each other - the jungle side towards the end near the ocean has an important but not necessary biome deep underground known as the shimmer, search it up if you want a deeper look)
- Prepare arenas for upcoming bosses and events

Mid Pre-Hardmode (Post Eye/Evil Boss/Queen Bee):
- Talk to that guy you may have met at the dungeon and summon his curse with your well-earned gear
- Explore the dungeons depths once you have beaten Skeletron
- Search the gold chests with the gold key drops (can drop from dungeon pots, dungeon enemies, dungeon slimes most commonly or rarely wood chests in the dungeon)
- Grab your dungeon loot alongside the possibility of an obsidian key to unlock those locked chests in hell if you've stumbled into there yet

9/10: Awesome game!!

I honestly can't believe I haven't left a review for this game yet. My one issue with Terraria is it can be rather grindy at times, especially if you want a specific item or weapon and sometimes the bosses can feel a little unfair when playing by yourself. Other than that, there is a reason it's been around for over 15 years and remains peak. The Villager Npc's feel a lot more than just shopkeepers having histories, lore, and even relationships with the other villagers. (which I love despite making it sometimes hard to plan houses for them all). This is definitely a game to play WITH friends, but can be just as fun with yourself. The vast amount of bosses, and weapons you can use to disperse them are definitely a huge plus, allowing for creative and often absurd solutions that fit for your playing style. 

I won't deny that you likely do need a wiki for progression or crafting while planning as while as cool as this game is, I won't deny that it isn't the most beginner friendly. (Personally I like that though). I feel it has a lot to offer, whether its building beautiful castles and creations, or battling against cosmic entities, or a fishing sim, there is something for everyone!

One of the Best games I have ever played.

The Gameplay is astounding. While it isn't 2D Minecraft by a long shot, they both share two things: Mining and Grinding. The Mining in this game is very fun, and the grind is there for people who really like making character builds.

This game has so many weapons, armors, abilities, and just items in general. It allows you to hyper-customize your character, its also why there are many kinds of challenge runs in Terraria (I never got into that stuff tho).

It has a clearly defined boss-based progression system that is very lenient with which boss you want to fight first, at least in pre-hardmode, and its a great progression system. It's very simple and very satisfying, to summarize it:
Get Equipment - Kill Boss - Get better Equipment - Kill harder Boss - Repeat until the game is over and you can kill anything in no time flat. 

Personally, I had an absolute blast playing this game, its combat and boss-battling is the heart of this game and it is awesome! The bosses are very well designed (design and in gameplay) and are just very unique, fun, and interesting to face

I had fun getting achievements, because some are challenging, some are easy, and some are silly, and some are bizarre.

This game is also great for its loads of content, not to mention how the devs actually are connected with the community and actually listen to us. It's amazing how far it's come.
